title: Turnover scheduling, contractor handover and property condition records
audience: Property managers and hosts who schedule cleaning, maintenance and inspections between short-stay bookings.
learningOutcomes: Schedule a turnover so that cleaning, laundry, maintenance and inspection fit the gap between bookings.
Record the property's condition at check-in and check-out so that damage can be separated from normal wear.
Hand over to contractors with the access, the scope and the limits of their authority written down.

instruction.heading: Build the schedule from the booking calendar
instruction.body: Start from the booking calendar, not from the cleaner's availability. Mark the checkout time, the next check-in time and the gap between them. Put the tasks that must be finished before the next guest arrives in order: the access check, the cleaning, the laundry and the inspection. Where a contractor's visit may be needed, book it before the gap is set, and keep a buffer for an inspection and any reinspection. Where the gap is too short for the work, tell the owner before accepting the next booking, rather than cutting the inspection short. The durations used for planning are business standards to be set by the owner and checked by the expert reviewer, not figures given in this lesson.

instruction.heading: Record the condition before and after each stay
instruction.body: Take dated photographs of each room, the appliances, the furnishings and the exterior at check-in and at check-out, and compare them. Record the meter readings where the owner requires them. Separate three kinds of finding: damage caused by a guest, which the owner may claim through the business's process; wear and tear that existed before the stay; and maintenance faults that need a repair. Do not describe a finding as guest damage unless the photographs, the inventory or the check-out record show it. Record the inventory of furnishings and supplies each time, so that missing items can be identified.

instruction.heading: Hand over to contractors with limits on their authority
instruction.body: Give each contractor the property address, the access arrangement for that visit, the job scope in writing, the time window, and the business contact for questions. State what the contractor may do without approval, such as replacing a bulb or clearing a drain, and what they must report and wait for approval before doing, such as replacing an appliance or any work on a structure. Ask for a written report and photographs at the end of each visit. Do not give a contractor access codes that remain valid after their visit, and do not allow them to hold keys beyond the visit period.

instruction.heading: Close the turnover
instruction.body: A turnover is closed when the cleaning, the laundry, the inspection and any repairs are recorded as complete or as not complete with a reason, the photographs are saved against the booking, and the next guest's access has been set. Do not mark a room as ready if any inspection item has not been done. Where work is incomplete, record what is outstanding, who is responsible, and the time it will be finished.

procedure: Read the booking calendar for the checkout time, the next check-in time and the gap between them.
Place the tasks in order: access check, cleaning, laundry, inspection, and any contractor visit, with a buffer for reinspection.
Tell the owner before accepting a booking if the gap is too short for the work.
Take dated photographs at check-in and check-out, and record the inventory and any meter readings the owner requires.
Separate guest damage, wear and tear, and maintenance faults, and record the evidence for each.
Give each contractor the address, access, written scope, time window and limits on their authority.
Collect the contractor's written report and photographs, and remove their access when the visit ends.
Close the turnover only when every task is recorded as complete or as not complete with a reason.

workedExamples.situation: A house has a checkout at 10:00 and a new guest arriving at 15:00. The laundry cycle and drying take longer than the gap allows, and the inspection has not been booked.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do with the booking calendar?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not start the laundry in a way that leaves the inspection out. Tell the owner that the gap is too short. Options to put to the owner include an earlier checkout confirmed with the guest, a later check-in if the guest agrees in writing, or an extra cleaner. Do not accept the check-in on the current plan until one is confirmed. Record the decision and who made it.

workedExamples.situation: At check-out, a sofa has a large stain and a broken leg. The check-in photographs were taken two weeks earlier and show the sofa without the stain.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you record the finding?
workedExamples.reasoning: Record the stain and the broken leg with dated photographs, and compare them with the check-in set. Do not state that the guest caused the damage until the evidence supports it. Record the item as a finding for the owner to decide, with the evidence attached. Do not repair or replace the sofa without the owner's approval.

equipmentAndPpe: Booking calendar showing checkout and check-in times.
Dated camera or phone photographs and the inventory sheet.
Contractor job sheet with scope, time window and limits on authority.

commonErrors.error: Planning the turnover around the cleaner's availability, not the booking gap.
commonErrors.prevention: Start from the booking calendar and place every task in order inside the gap.

commonErrors.error: Describing a finding as guest damage without evidence.
commonErrors.prevention: Compare with the check-in record and attach the photographs before recording a cause.

commonErrors.error: Giving a contractor access that stays valid after the visit.
commonErrors.prevention: Set access for the visit period only and remove it when the visit ends.

commonErrors.error: Closing a turnover with an inspection not done.
commonErrors.prevention: Record every task as complete or as not complete with a reason before closing.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Any work on electrical, gas, plumbing or structural items must be done by a person authorised for that work. A contractor's visit does not make the host or the cleaner authorised for that work. Licence and authorisation requirements vary by state and territory and are UNCONFIRMED here. Flagged for expert review.

Where a guest may have been injured or property has been damaged in a way that may lead to a claim, record the facts and the photographs and refer the matter to the business owner before anyone discusses it with the guest.
Insurance claims and the owner's rights to recover costs from guests depend on the policy and the booking terms. They are UNCONFIRMED in this lesson. Flagged for expert review.

qualityStandard: Every turnover has a schedule that fits the booking gap, with a buffer for inspection.
Every check-in and check-out has dated photographs and an inventory record.
Every contractor visit has a written scope, a time window, a written report and removed access after the visit.
documentationEvidence: Turnover schedule with checkout, check-in, task times and buffer.
Dated check-in and check-out photographs, inventory and any meter readings the owner requires.
Contractor job sheet, written report and access record.
summary: Plan the turnover from the booking gap, and tell the owner early if the gap is too short.
Compare check-in and check-out records before recording any damage.
Limit contractor access and authority to the visit and the written scope.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should set the order of the turnover tasks?
options: The booking gap, with the tasks that must finish first placed earliest
The order of the rooms on the floor plan

knowledgeChecks.question: At check-out a finding is not in the check-in photographs. What is the right record?
options: Record it as guest damage straight away
Record the finding with the dated evidence, and let the owner decide the cause
Ignore it, because the guest may not have been responsible

knowledgeChecks.question: A contractor finds an electrical fault during a visit for a bulb change. What is the correct step?
options: Repair the fault, because the visit is already booked
Report the fault in writing and wait for approval for work outside the written scope
Let the next guest report it
